events.title: What Does Wilderness Dream Of?

The canvases and the works on paper

The main room — paintings first, sculpture between
Wall text at the entrance sets up the show
Close — closed Sundays

events.title: The IIC Experience 2026 — opens

cost.note: Free. No ticket, no registration — walk in and sit.

events.what_happens: A quiet opening. The exhibition in the Annexe is up from 4 pm and people drift between that and the main building; at 6:30 everyone settles into the auditorium for the keynote — roughly an hour of illustrated lecture, then questions. The evening breaks up around 8.

run_of_show.what: Exhibition opens in the Annexe gallery — South Asian texts and traditions
Keynote in the C.D. Deshmukh Auditorium: Naman P. Ahuja on tree worship in Indian art
Questions from the floor
Hall empties; people drift back to the exhibition

practical.worth_knowing: Runs daily to 6 November, so there's no urgency.

events.title: Qawwali at Nizamuddin Dargah
events.summary: Starts around sunset in the courtyard of the 14th-century shrine and builds from a slow alap into a full ensemble with harmonium and dholak. Cover your head, leave shoes at the…
events.description: Sufi poetry in Urdu and Persian, sung to build toward trance — mostly Amir Khusrau and other Chishti-lineage poets, in praise of the saint and of God.
events.address: Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya Dargah, Nizamuddin West, New Delhi 110013

cost.note: Free, no ticket. Head covered, shoes off at the lane.

events.what_happens: The qawwals sit cross-legged with harmonium, dholak and tabla and start low — one voice over a drone — then build verse by verse until the whole party is singing and the audience is clapping the beat. People sit on the floor in a ring; the crowd thickens as it gets louder.

run_of_show.what: Qawwals settle in cross-legged; harmonium, dholak and tabla tune up
One voice over a drone — the slow opening
Verses build, the full party singing, audience clapping the beat
Peak, then a wind-down

events.food: Nothing at the dargah itself. The lane outside is full of kebab and biryani shops — eat before or after.

practical.entry: Free, no ticket. Head covered, shoes off at the lane.
practical.getting_there: JLN Stadium (Violet) or Jangpura, then a short auto — ask for the dargah gate, not the basti.
practical.how_long: 60–90 minutes from sunset; longer on Urs nights.
practical.worth_knowing: Thursdays only. Women may enter the courtyard but not the inner chamber.

verification.note: Weekly listing; the page rolls to the next occurrence.

events.gist: You sit on the floor in a courtyard and listen to live qawwali — harmonium, dholak, tabla and voices — for an hour or more. Standing at the back is fine too.

events.title: Sarangbang — the Korean scholar's room

run_of_show.what: Hall opens
The room itself, viewed from the threshold
Wall texts on the scholar's day and each object
Close — weekdays only, shut at weekends

events.food: Nothing at IGNCA; Connaught Place is a fifteen-minute walk.

practical.getting_there: Udyog Bhawan (Yellow) or Shivaji Stadium (Airport Express), then a short walk.

verification.note: Not re-checked against the organiser since the date above.

Slow walk between the tombs, stopping at calls and hollows
Run-through of what was spotted

Close
